stories.title: Western allies slam Israel for ending World Central Kitchen strike probe
stories.summary: UK, Australia and Canada call Israel’s decision not to investigate deadly 2024 strike on a Gaza aid convoy ‘shameful’. The United Kingdom, Australia and Canada have called Israel’s decision not to pursue a criminal investigation into its deadly strike on a World Central Kitchen aid convoy in Gaza “shameful”. In a joint statement released on Friday, the three countries’ foreign ministries called on Israel to comply with international humanitarian law, saying they had spent more than two years pressing Israel to hold those responsible for the drone strike in central Gaza accountable. “This decision is both too little, and too late. The victims of this incident and their families deserve justice and accountability, and we will continue to seek answers on their behalf,” the statement said. Seven World Central Kitchen aid workers – three Britons, a dual US-Canadian national, a Pole, an Australian, and a Palestinian – were killed in their convoy after overseeing a food aid shipment in April 2024. In a separate statement on Friday, Poland’s foreign ministry said it was “very disappointed” in Israel’s decision to not investigate the drone strike. The ministry also said that it has summoned Israel’s ambassador in Warsaw after the Israeli military made the announcement. Australia also summoned Israel’s ambassador in Canberra on Thursday. Israel’s military called the deadly strike a “tragic mistake”. But it announced on Wednesday that it would not launch investigations into the attack that killed the aid workers from the celebrity chef Jose Andres’ World Central Kitchen. The announcement came after a review of 150 incidents of Israeli troop conduct during its genocidal war on Gaza, including the killing of Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian child.

stories.title: Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz fires economy minister amid unrest
stories.summary: Jose Gabriel Espinoza removed from post days after he was censured by the legislature amid tumult over economic reform. Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz has removed Economic Minister Jose Gabriel Espinoza from his post after the minister was censured by the country’s Congress. The cabinet shake-up is likely to be perceived as a concession by Paz, who has faced public anger about the country’s ongoing cost-of-living crisis. The announcement came in a decree published on Friday in the government’s official gazette. It names Oscar Mario Justiniano Pinto as interim economy minister and explains he will serve in the role until a permanent candidate is appointed. The decree does not, however, offer a prospective timeline for the eventual replacement. The decision to fire Espinoza, however, marks a reversal for the Paz government. On Tuesday, the Bolivian Congress voted to censure Espinoza, after he failed to appear before the legislature to answer questions about the economy. Under the country’s constitution, a censure tees up a subsequent dismissal. The right-wing Paz administration initially said it would fight that decision as a tribunal reviewed the dispute. But Friday’s decree suggests the president changed course. Bolivia has been roiled by economic and political turmoil for years.

stories.title: German politician warns against further escalating Ukrainian conflict
stories.summary: Sahra Wagenknecht noted that German technologies and German money are used to attack Moscow
article_sentences: BERLIN, August 21.

Sahra Wagenknecht, the leader of Germany’s BSW party (formerly known as Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance - Reason and Justice party) has called for ending the escalation of the Ukrainian conflict and warned that, in the event of a major European war, hostilities would take place primarily in Germany.
In an interview with the Funke media group, she noted that British drones are being used to strike Russia.
"German technologies and German money are used to attack Moscow.
From Russia’s viewpoint, NATO has long been waging a war against it," she said.
"If we don’t stop this dangerous escalation, we will soon find ourselves in a situation of a major European war that will be fought primarily on German territory."

"The fact that [German Chancellor] Friedrich Merz wants to turn Germany into Europe’s greatest military power again and, at the same time, recklessly allows for the possibility that we might be drawn into a war with a nuclear power is a clear violation of the obligation to preserve peace, as enshrined in the fundamental law," she stressed, adding that Russia is trying to prevent the deployment of NATO troops and missiles near its borders.
She also spoke against shutting down the Russia House in Berlin some German politicians and political forces have been increasingly calling for.
"What have the sanctions imposed until today brought about?
Should we dismantle the last remaining bridges of exchanges and mutual understanding?" she said.
"It is precisely in times of war and tension that we need more dialogue, not less.
Russia has been and remains our largest European neighbor, the country that once made the unification [of the country] possible and with which we must live in peace.".

stories.title: China mulls over bid to host 2028 UN climate talks, sources say
stories.summary: China is considering hosting the 2028 UN climate talks (COP33) to enhance its image as a leader in fighting global warming, though no final decision or timeline has been made. Hosting COP33 could strengthen China's climate credentials amid US-China tensions, especially as the summit would occur shortly after the 2028 US presidential election. China faces scrutiny as the world's largest greenhouse gas emitter, with modest emission reduction targets by 2035 despite pledging carbon neutrality by 2060. China is mulling a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028, two sources familiar with the matter told AFP on Aug 21, as it seeks to burnish its reputation as a leader in the fight against global warming. Beijing has not yet made a final decision regarding the proposal for the COP33 summit, both sources said, nor is there a clear timeline for doing so. The host does not have to be decided this year. China’s interest was first reported by Bloomberg News. The UN’s annual climate gatherings rotate among regional blocs. This year’s COP31 is scheduled to take place in Turkey, followed by COP32 in Ethiopia in 2027. The 2028 summit falls to the Asia-Pacific. In April, India withdrew its offer to host COP33 without specifying a reason. South Korea has previously expressed interest.

stories.summary: The federal government finally has a new plan for the shrinking Colorado River. It spells out which states will have to use less water over the next two years.
